entry.evidence: In this paper, we propose a novel picking algorithm for the automatic P- and S-waves onset time determination.

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML text (jats_text), checked against the published PDF

steps.action: Frame the need for automatic, robust, computationally light pickers of P- and S-arrival times for monitoring and early warning.
steps.quote: automatic picking algorithms capable of carrying out a precise and reliable identification of the arrival times of seismic phases has become increasingly important

steps.action: Review existing pickers (Allen CF, Baer-Kradolfer, higher-order statistics, AR-AIC) and the shortcomings reported by comparative studies by other groups.
steps.quote: A comparative study by Küperkoch et al. (19) shows that this algorithm tends to pick somewhat early compared to what an analyst would pick.

steps.action: Adopt the co-author's earlier changepoint method for variance piecewise constant models (Adelfio 2012) as the basis for onset picking.
steps.quote: In this paper, we advocate the usage of the algorithm proposed in Adelfio (1) for the automated seismogram onset time determination.

steps.action: Report the authors' earlier synthetic tests (D'Angelo et al. 2020, 2021): good P and S detection, but the post-selection step sometimes picked the wrong changepoints.
steps.quote: it is noticed that the post-selection algorithm is not always able to correctly identify the relevant changepoints

steps.action: Set out the model: variance changes recast as mean changes of squared studentized residuals, a gamma GLM with log link, a cumSeg-type segmented fit, lars selection and a generalized BIC.
steps.quote: a gamma generalized linear model (GLM) is fitted with a log-link function, with response given by the squared studentized residuals

steps.action: Fix the BIC constant Cn = log log n on the basis of the authors' earlier simulation comparison of specifications.
steps.quote: Thus, we use this value for the provided analysis.

steps.action: Propose changepost, which selects among the estimated changepoints the two with the largest variance ratios as the P and S arrivals (Algorithm 1).
steps.quote: The two relevant changepoints are selected as the two ones in correspondence to the two biggest variance ratios.

steps.action: Check changepost on a toy simulated signal with known piecewise variance (Figs. 1-2).
steps.quote: it is evident that changepost correctly identifies the changepoints corresponding to the most abrupt changes in the variance.

steps.action: Design a validation on synthetic seismograms with known arrival times: 12 scenarios (distances 10, 50 and 250 km by magnitudes 2-5), 100 waveforms each, vertical component only.
steps.quote: for controlling the precision and accuracy of an automatic picking procedure, the best practice is to start from simulated data

steps.action: Generate broadband synthetic waveforms by a hybrid SPECFEM3D low-frequency and empirical Green's function high-frequency approach (Fig. 3).
steps.quote: The seismic waveforms are simulated using the deterministic hybrid approach proposed by Mourhatch and Krishnan (21).

steps.action: Apply changepost to every synthetic waveform; report the mean and MSE of the estimated P and S arrivals and the share of waveforms with no estimate (Table 1).
steps.quote: Table 1 reports the empirical means (m) and Mean Squared Error values (s) of the two relevant changepoints estimated by the proposed algorithm

steps.action: Examine how performance varies across the magnitude and distance scenarios; changepost fails entirely at 250 km for M2-3 and is best at 10 km.
steps.quote: the NA values are most likely to occur when the magnitude is small and the distance is large

steps.action: Set up the STA/LTA baseline (Allen 1978), tuning window lengths and thresholds per distance class through optimization tests (Table 2).
steps.quote: After several optimization tests for each earthquake class, we set the parameters reported in Table 2 for the comparison.

steps.action: Run STA/LTA on the same synthetics, keep the pick closest to the truth, and compare its mean, MSE and NA% with changepost (Tables 1 and 3).
steps.quote: We have noticed that the number of the picked arrival times is generally lower using the STA/LTA

steps.action: Revise the comparison metric: because many candidate picks bias the MSE in favour of changepost, define a probability index of picks within ±0.2 s of the truth.
steps.quote: Therefore, we define a probability index, computed for each waveform q:

steps.action: Compare the probability indices (Tables 4 and 5) and computational cost: STA/LTA is better on P, changepost on S; changepost is slower but not prohibitively so.
steps.quote: Overall, changepost outperforms STA/LTA in the S-Phases picking. Otherwise, the STA/LTA picking time is better for the P-Phases

steps.action: Assemble real waveforms from the 2009 L'Aquila sequence (80 events, 12 stations, 2880 traces), bandpass-filtered at 0.1-35 Hz and normalized.
steps.quote: The complete database is made up of 80 seismic events recorded by 12 stations with three components

steps.action: Apply changepost (K* = 10) and STA/LTA, with the Table 2 settings, to real waveforms and compare picks visually on five traces from station BSSO (Figs. 4-5), with no reference picks.
steps.quote: while changepost is always able to identify two arrival times

steps.action: Keep the claim that changepost is flexible and needs no testing or optimization phase, unlike STA/LTA.
steps.quote: These results confirm the conclusion drawn by simulation study, that is the high flexibility of the proposed changepost algorithm.

Partly: performance degrades with distance and low magnitude and fails at 250 km for M2-3; real-data check is visual only
Kept: method characterized as comparable to STA/LTA (worse on P, better on S) and tuning-free

end.claim: The changepost algorithm automatically picks P- and S-wave onsets with performance similar to a tuned STA/LTA on synthetic seismograms (less precise on P, better on S), and needs no testing or optimization phase.

decisive_move.sentence: The comparison of changepost and tuned STA/LTA picks against the known synthetic arrival times, with the probability index, is what characterizes the method's performance.

gates.evidence: No hypothesis directed data acquisition: synthetic scenarios were chosen to map performance (§3 ¶2), and the real L'Aquila data were an archive application. The synthetic accuracy claim faced known truth and could fail; it did fail at 250 km for M2-3 (Table 1) and lost to STA/LTA on P (§3.3 ¶7). The headline flexibility claim rests on five real traces with no reference picks (§4 ¶2-3). Cn = log log n was fixed from earlier simulations before these data (§2 ¶6), but the STA/LTA parameters were tuned on the synthetic test data (§3.3 ¶4), and no analysis plan was registered.

novelty_claims.quote: In this paper, we propose a novel picking algorithm for the automatic P- and S-waves onset time determination.
This section proposes a new methodology for automatic picking of arrival times based on the theory of the variance piecewise constant models.
Indeed, changepost is entirely automatic, meaning that no choice of any parameters is needed to run the algorithm.

limits: The real-data application has no reference (analyst) picks. Only five waveforms from one station (BSSO) are shown, and no quantitative metric is given for the 2880 traces, so the claim that accuracy is 'almost independent of the analyzed dataset' (§4 ¶3) is asserted, not tested. Sub-claim statuses: tuning-free flexibility on real data, status none (asserted, untested); changepost better on S and worse on P than STA/LTA on synthetics, capability_characterized within the 12 scenarios. The STA/LTA settings were tuned on the synthetics (200 Hz) and reused unchanged on the 100 Hz real data, which handicaps the baseline on real data. The abstract's 'similar results' glosses over STA/LTA's better P precision (Tables 4-5). The Fig. 4 and Fig. 5 captions say three events but each shows five panels. Only the vertical component is reported. All synthetics have impulsive onsets, so emergent onsets are untested. Computational time is described qualitatively only. The default 'No conclusion' for 250 km M2-3 is left unexplained beyond signal-to-noise. It is inference that changepost revises the post-selection step criticized in D'Angelo et al. 2021; the paper does not say what changed. Code and data are available only on request. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.
